title: Aircall vs Unitel Voice — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Aircall vs Unitel Voice for Small Teams
description: Aircall and Unitel Voice compared for very small teams: entry prices, cost for three people, minimums and guarantees, and HubSpot call logging.
dek: A CRM-connected call center and a lean virtual phone system, compared for a team of one to three people who need a real business number.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown. Both links are affiliate links.

blocks.html: This comparison is for a founder, a consultant, or a team of up to three who want a business phone number that isn't someone's cell, and are weighing {{link:aircall}} against {{link:unitel-voice}}.

These two tools solve different problems. One is a calling platform built to sit inside a CRM like {{link:hubspot}}. The other is a virtual phone system that gives a small business a main number, extensions, and routing for very little money.

Choose Unitel Voice if you need a professional number and call routing and don't need calls in a CRM. Choose Aircall if every call should land on the HubSpot record and the team will grow into a sales or support line.
For three people, Aircall Essentials comes to about {{calc:aircall_three}} a month on annual billing. Unitel Voice Office is {{fact:unitel.office_price}}.

Aircall Essentials is {{fact:aircall.essentials_annual}}, and Professional is {{fact:aircall.professional_license}}. There's {{fact:aircall.min_licenses_ess_pro}}, and you get {{fact:aircall.annual_saving}}. {{fact:aircall.power_dialer}}.
Unitel Voice Solo is {{fact:unitel.solo_price}}. Team is {{fact:unitel.team_price}}. Office is {{fact:unitel.office_price}}, with {{fact:unitel.extra_user}}.
Unitel Voice offers a {{fact:unitel.guarantee}}. Recording isn't included by default: {{fact:unitel.call_recording}}.
If you're one person who needs a main line that rings your cell, Unitel Voice's Solo plan is built for that and costs a fraction of a calling platform.
If two or three people make sales calls and you want notes, recordings, and outcomes on the HubSpot contact, Aircall's HubSpot logging is the reason to pay more.
Aircall's three-license minimum makes it expensive for a solo founder, and the price climbs quickly past Essentials.
Unitel Voice doesn't list a HubSpot integration on the facts checked here, so calls won't land on CRM records by themselves, and recording is an add-on.
Ask whether calls are a sales channel or simply how customers reach you. If they're a sales channel, buy the tool that logs to HubSpot. If not, buy the cheap, reliable line.
Both have a way to back out: Aircall bills monthly if you skip the annual discount, and Unitel Voice has a money-back window.
